# Message codes: Options

See also: [Message codes](message-codes.md) (the index of every code) and
[Messages and codes](messages.md) (the line grammar, what a code guarantees and
when to trust one).

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`message-codes-values.md` the values.

## Codes

| Code | Level | Means | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`option-conflict`](#option-conflict) | ERROR | The command line holds an option the command cannot take in this case (-o/--output with several wheels), or one an existing ID registry contradicts: 'loom id generate --namespace' for a registry made with another namespace, or 'loom id generate' with a --project-dir (the current directory when not given), or 'loom id import' with an explicit one, other than the one the registry was made for. The 'not allowed with' line is reserved for options of a mutually exclusive group; no command has one yet. | 0.25.0 |
| [`option-invalid`](#option-invalid) | ERROR | The command line holds an option or a value the command does not take: an unknown option, a value of the wrong form or out of range, an unknown subcommand, an option out of order (a creator's type or email before its name), or a 'loom id generate' PATH outside --project-dir (the library: a path outside the project root given to IdRegistry.generate). Or a library caller gave a value of the wrong type or shape (the must-be line, as config-invalid says it of a setting: a byte cap of 0, a creation_datetime that is no ISO 8601 date, an empty SBOM given to embed_sbom_in_wheel). Or a document namespace given as --namespace or to IdRegistry is not an absolute IRI without a '#' (the namespace lines, also the detail of 'argument --namespace:'); one holding a credential is credentials-unsafe/registry on both. Or a URL credential fingerprint given to the library is not one; the line never shows the value, which may be a credential pasted by mistake. Or PitloomConfig.url_credentials is neither warn nor refuse, or CredentialPolicy(refuse=...) is no bool. The same faults in [tool.pitloom] are config-invalid. An option given without its value is option-missing; two options argparse refuses together are option-conflict. | 0.25.0 |

Said once per value and process. | 0.25.0 |

### `option-conflict`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: The command line holds an option the command cannot take in this
  case (-o/--output with several wheels), or one an existing ID registry
  contradicts: 'loom id generate --namespace' for a registry made with another
  namespace, or 'loom id generate' with a --project-dir (the current directory
  when not given), or 'loom id import' with an explicit one, other than the one
  the registry was made for. The 'not allowed with' line is reserved for options
  of a mutually exclusive group; no command has one yet.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Ran nothing: the command exits 1 (2 for the 'not allowed
  with' line), the library (IdRegistry) raises ValueError carrying the code, and
  an ID registry is left as it is.
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may drop the option, run the command once
  per input, or, for an ID registry, pass the namespace or project directory the
  registry holds (or name another registry file), and run again. Deleting a
  registry to change them loses every id it pins: that is the user's decision,
  never the caller's.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: <option> cannot be used <when> [option-conflict]
  ERROR: argument <option>: not allowed with argument <other> [option-conflict]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: namespace <namespace> is not --namespace <given-namespace>; delete it to change the namespace [option-conflict]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: namespace <namespace> is not --namespace <given-namespace> (they differ in masked credentials); delete it to change the namespace [option-conflict]
  ERROR: ID registry: FILE=<file>: project root '<path>' is not '<root>'; delete it to change the project root [option-conflict]
  ```

### `option-invalid`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: The command line holds an option or a value the command does not
  take: an unknown option, a value of the wrong form or out of range, an unknown
  subcommand, an option out of order (a creator's type or email before its
  name), or a 'loom id generate' PATH outside --project-dir (the library: a path
  outside the project root given to IdRegistry.generate). Or a library caller
  gave a value of the wrong type or shape (the must-be line, as config-invalid
  says it of a setting: a byte cap of 0, a creation_datetime that is no ISO 8601
  date, an empty SBOM given to embed_sbom_in_wheel). Or a document namespace
  given as --namespace or to IdRegistry is not an absolute IRI without a '#'
  (the namespace lines, also the detail of 'argument --namespace:'); one holding
  a credential is credentials-unsafe/registry on both. Or a URL credential
  fingerprint given to the library is not one; the line never shows the value,
  which may be a credential pasted by mistake. Or PitloomConfig.url_credentials
  is neither warn nor refuse, or CredentialPolicy(refuse=...) is no bool. The
  same faults in [tool.pitloom] are config-invalid. An option given without its
  value is option-missing; two options argparse refuses together are
  option-conflict.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Ran nothing: the command exits 2 (the Action step fails), 1
  for a PATH outside --project-dir; the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code for a build timeout out of range (BuildOptions), a path outside the
  project root (IdRegistry.generate), a value of the wrong type or shape
  (ProvenanceConfig and PitloomConfig refuse a bad provenance format, schema or
  detail when built), a namespace that is none (IdRegistry), a fingerprint that
  is none (CredentialPolicy) or a url-credentials that is no mode; a loom SDK
  call raises TypeError carrying the code for an argument of the wrong type,
  ValueError for an unknown dataset_type.
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may fix the option or value the line names
  ('loom <command> --help' lists them) and run again. Tell the user only when
  the value came from them. For a fingerprint, the user copies it from the
  credentials-unsafe/written or refused line that offers it; do not show the
  value they gave, and do not edit their configuration.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: argument <option>: <refusal> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: unrecognized arguments: <error> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: ambiguous option: <error> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: build timeout must be 1-<limit> seconds, got <value> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: PATH '<path>' is outside --project-dir '<root>' [option-invalid]
  ERROR: ID registry: PATH '<path>' is not inside the project root '<root>' [option-invalid]
  ERROR: not a fingerprint (sha256: and 16 to 64 lowercase hex digits) [option-invalid]
  ERROR: <option>: must be <expected>, got <got> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: loom SDK: <option>: must be <expected>, got <got> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: namespace <why>: <namespace> [option-invalid]
  ERROR: namespace is empty [option-invalid]
  ```

### `option-missing`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: The command line lacks an argument or option the command needs (a
  subcommand, -o/--output for 'loom generate', an ID registry for 'loom id'), or
  the value of an option given (-o with nothing after it). The loom SDK line is
  a call that needs one made before it in the run.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Ran nothing: the command exits 2 (a parse error) or 1; the
  loom SDK raises RuntimeError carrying the code (a with block it leaves writes
  nothing).
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may add what the line names and run again.
  Tell the user only when the value must come from them (an output file, a
  registry location).
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: the following arguments are required: <error> [option-missing]
  ERROR: argument <option>: expected <arity> [option-missing]
  ERROR: -o/--output is required: a detected target has no default file name; pass -o FILE, or use 'loom project', 'loom wheel', 'loom model' or 'loom env' for that target's own default [option-missing]
  ERROR: no ID registry declared: pass --id-registry FILE or set id-registry in <table> [option-missing]
  ERROR: loom SDK: no model set; call set_model() or use_model() first [option-missing]
  ```

### `option-missing/project-dir`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: 'loom embed-wheel' ran without --project-dir in a directory holding
  a pyproject.toml: it never reads a project it is not given, so the SBOM it
  embeds is built from the wheel's own files and METADATA.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Built the SBOM from the wheel alone and embedded it; the exit
  status does not change.
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may run again with --project-dir naming the
  project the wheel was built from, for an SBOM that also states what the
  project declares (its lock file, its configuration).
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: --project-dir not given; the SBOM is built from the wheel alone, not from the project in the current directory [option-missing/project-dir]
  ```

### `option-no-effect`

- **Level**: WARNING, INFO.
- **Means**: An option or setting was given that the target or command cannot
  act on (a build flag without --allow-build, --use-lockfile for a wheel given
  to 'loom generate', a library parameter a URL target ignores); the line says
  why, naming each option as the surface that ran spells it: a flag on the
  command line (--build-timeout), a parameter in the library
  (BuildOptions.timeout, use_lockfile). The INFO: line is a [tool.pitloom]
  setting the build hook or 'embed-wheel' never acts on, named by its TOML key
  (tool.pitloom.describe-relationship). The FINGERPRINT= line is a fingerprint
  accepted (--accept-url-credential, accept-url-credentials in [tool.pitloom])
  that no URL value of the SBOM it names (its document id) has: a value since
  removed, or a fingerprint mistyped. The DIR= line is 'loom id generate' or
  'loom id import' given -o and --project-dir, whose project config could not be
  read (a bare setup(), an invalid setting): its url-credentials is not applied.
  The FILE= line is a --config file (loom.run's pitloom_config) with no
  [tool.pitloom] table: a wrong file, most often.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Ran as if it were not given; the run goes on.
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may drop the option from its command, or
  pick the target or companion option it needs (the line says which). Nothing to
  tell the user unless they asked for the option; for the INFO: line, do not
  edit their configuration. For the FINGERPRINT= line, tell the user the
  acceptance accepts nothing here; they may drop it. For the DIR= line, tell the
  user the project's url-credentials was not applied and why; to refuse, the
  caller adds --refuse-url-credentials. For the FILE= line, the caller checks it
  named the file it meant.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: Options: <name>: <option> has no effect <when> [option-no-effect]
  INFO: Options: <name>: <option> has no effect <when> [option-no-effect]
  WARNING: Build: <name>: <option> has no effect <when> [option-no-effect]
  WARNING: Options: FINGERPRINT=<fingerprint>: matches no URL of the SBOM <element> [option-no-effect]
  WARNING: Options: DIR=<dir>: url-credentials not read: <failure>; the warn mode applies; add <option> to refuse [option-no-effect]
  WARNING: Options: FILE=<file>: <option> has no [tool.pitloom] table; the defaults apply [option-no-effect]
  ```

### `sbom-name-invalid`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An SBOM base name (sbom-basename in a configuration file,
  --sbom-basename, a library caller's sbom_basename) has white space around it
  or ends in .spdx3.json (any case), which every writer adds itself. Said once
  per value and process.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Used the base name the line names (white space and one
  trailing .spdx3.json taken off): the SBOM file is named <value>.spdx3.json.
- **Nothing to do**: Nothing to do: the file is named as intended. To silence
  the line, give the base name without white space and without .spdx3.json.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: <config-key>: <got> is not a bare file name (white space or a trailing .spdx3.json); using <base-name> [sbom-name-invalid]
  WARNING: <option>: <got> is not a bare file name (white space or a trailing .spdx3.json); using <base-name> [sbom-name-invalid]
  ```
